technical_and_design_decisions: Port the modules as Spring-compatible components in the existing s-c-s repository while preserving the observable behavior and configuration semantics of the corresponding Spring XD modules.
Use the repository's existing build system, module layout, dependency-management conventions, coding standards, and supported Java/Spring versions wherever available.
Implement router, file, FTP, Redis, and GemFire as sink modules, and Rabbit as a source module, matching the directions stated in the user stories.
Prefer existing Spring Integration, Spring Data Redis, Spring AMQP, Spring Integration FTP, Spring Integration File, and GemFire integrations rather than introducing custom transport implementations.
Keep module configuration externally configurable through the repository's established property or metadata mechanism and provide module metadata for pipeline composition.
Use unit tests with mocks and local test doubles for module behavior, supplemented by integration tests where an embedded or locally available service is practical.
Treat HDP/PHD support as dependency, configuration, and compatibility updates for HDFS-related functionality rather than implementing a new Hadoop client.
Document migration behavior and incompatibilities in repository documentation, with explicit sections for configuration changes, removed or changed features, and upgrade actions.
assumptions: The existing XD module source code, build files, and relevant tests are available for inspection and can be legally reused or adapted in the s-c-s repository.
The s-c-s repository already provides a working parent build and conventions for creating source and sink modules; only module-specific adaptation and integration work is required.
The requested increment requires functional parity with the XD modules, not additional features beyond compatibility with the target repository.
The target runtime is Java 17 or later and uses the Spring Framework version supported by the target s-c-s repository.
No major redesign of the s-c-s pipeline runtime, deployment model, or public module API is required.

External services such as RabbitMQ, Redis, FTP, HDFS, and GemFire may not be continuously available; unavailable systems will be tested using mocks, embedded services, or documented compatibility checks.
HDP and PHD version requirements can be satisfied through supported client-library and configuration updates without requiring changes to an actual production cluster.
The migration section covers releases 1.2 to 1.3 and is based on repository history, dependency differences, module behavior, and known backward incompatibilities.
Effort includes implementation, developer testing, code review preparation, documentation, and build verification, but excludes project management and production deployment.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the s-c-s repository structure, build conventions, runtime APIs, module metadata, existing tests, and the corresponding XD implementations. Identify dependencies, configuration mappings, compatibility risks, and the migration scope for all eight user stories.
Create or adapt module projects, parent-build entries, dependency declarations, packaging configuration, metadata, and baseline configuration needed to host the ported modules in s-c-s.

Port the router module from XD as an s-c-s sink, adapt its message-routing behavior and configuration, integrate it with the target runtime, and add focused unit tests for routing rules and error cases.
Port the file sink module, including destination handling, file naming and writing behavior, configuration properties, lifecycle behavior, error handling, metadata, and module-level tests.

Port the FTP sink module, adapt FTP session and transfer configuration to the target APIs, preserve connection and error semantics, provide metadata, and implement unit tests using mocked or local FTP interactions.

Move the Redis sink implementation into s-c-s, update Redis client and Spring integration dependencies as needed, preserve serialization and key/value behavior, and add unit tests for supported operations and configuration.

Move the Rabbit source module into s-c-s, adapt listener, acknowledgement, conversion, and connection configuration to the target runtime, provide source metadata, and add tests for message consumption and failure handling.
Move the GemFire sink module, adapt client and region interaction to supported Spring/GemFire APIs, preserve mapping and write behavior, handle connection failures, and add focused unit tests.

Update Hadoop/HDFS-related dependencies, version properties, configuration, and compatibility code for the latest supported HDP and PHD distributions. Verify dependency resolution and document supported versions and limitations.

Add and execute repository-level tests covering module discovery, packaging, pipeline wiring, serialization, configuration binding, startup/shutdown behavior, and representative end-to-end flows for the migrated source and sink modules.

Create the 1.2-to-1.3 migration section, compare dependencies and module behavior, document new improvements, identify backward incompatibilities, and provide actionable upgrade and configuration guidance.

activities.activity_name: Quality, CI, packaging, and final verification
activities.activity_description: Run formatting and static checks, resolve build and dependency issues, verify clean builds and artifacts, update CI or test configuration where necessary, review documentation and metadata, and prepare the complete increment for submission.
